defects.summary: A CVSS baseScore with a huge exponent raises decimal.Overflow out of `cve.normalize` instead of PT-ENRICH-PROVIDER.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/enrichment/cve.py:193-196 (`Decimal(value) * 10` guarded only by InvalidOperation); callers catch EnrichmentError only: src/patchtrace/cli.py:392-407 and :472
defects.failure_scenario: An NVD (or MSRC) response carrying `"baseScore": 1E+1000000` (number or string). normalize() raises decimal.Overflow (reproduced with python -c, also for the string form). In `correlate --fetch` the exception is not an EnrichmentError, so `_normalize_available` cannot fall back to the other provider and the snapshots of every other requested CVE are discarded; the generic handler ends the command (CLI consequence by code reading; the provider hosts are unreachable here).
defects.proposed_fix: Catch decimal.ArithmeticError (or use a local decimal context without traps and test is_finite / range first) in _tenths and raise _err(...).
defects.regression_test: tests/test_enrichment_cve.py: parametrized baseScore in (1E+1000000, "1E+1000000") expects EnrichmentError PT-ENRICH-PROVIDER; tests/test_enrichment_review_regressions.py: batch survives one such response

defects.summary: An imported CVE snapshot whose retrieved_at lies at the edge of the datetime range passes `parse_snapshots` but raises OverflowError in `is_stale`.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/enrichment/cve.py:394 (`_timestamp(...).astimezone(UTC)`); accepted by cve.py:170-174; consumer src/patchtrace/enrichment/pipeline.py:351-355 catches EnrichmentError only
defects.failure_scenario: `patchtrace correlate PROJECT --cve CVE-2024-0001 --snapshot bad.json` where retrieved_at is "0001-01-01T00:00:00+05:00" (or "9999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00"): prints "error: OverflowError: date value out of range", exit 3, no contextual result (reproduced on a sample project).
defects.proposed_fix: Make _timestamp normalise to UTC inside its try (OverflowError -> PT-ENRICH-INPUT) so parse_snapshots rejects the file with the snapshot index; is_stale then cannot overflow.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_enrichment_cve.py: both boundary stamps rejected by parse_snapshots with PT-ENRICH-INPUT

defects.summary: CVE identifier normalisation differs per verb: `correlate --cve` rejects lower case and surrounding space, while `intelligence --cve` strips and upper-cases and `kev lookup` upper-cases ASCII tokens.

defects.summary: KEV store provenance is last-writer-wins for a non-current snapshot and first-writer-wins for the current one: re-installing identical bytes from another source silently replaces (or keeps) the meta, losing the TLS authenticity and the consent record, and the service reports a description the store does not hold.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/kev/store.py:327-329 (meta published unconditionally), :315-318 (unchanged branch returns before any provenance comparison); src/patchtrace/kev/service.py:91-95 (`in_use = meta if result.current_id == meta.snapshot_id`)
defects.failure_scenario: Reproduced with kev-synthetic-2099.json: (C) fetched from cisa-site, a newer release installed, then the same old bytes imported from a local file -> meta/<id>.json changes from cisa-site/tls-allowlisted-host with consent to local-import/unverified-local-file with consent=None. (B) local import current, then the same bytes fetched over TLS -> outcome unchanged, store still says unverified-local-file while Installed.in_use (shown by `kev fetch`) says cisa-site.
defects.proposed_fix: Before publishing the meta, read the existing one for that snapshot id: never replace a tls-allowlisted-host meta with a local-import one; allow the upgrade local -> TLS (also in the unchanged branch); make the service return the stored meta. Record the rule in docs/specs/kev-exploitation-context.md first.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_kev_store.py: test_reimport_never_downgrades_provenance, test_fetch_upgrades_a_local_import; tests/test_kev_service.py: Installed.in_use equals store.read_meta

defects.summary: `correlate --save-snapshot` writes with Path.write_text after the network fetch: not atomic and the target is not checked first.
defects.failure_scenario: Target directory missing: the fetch (64 CVEs can take minutes of NVD pacing) completes, then "error: FileNotFoundError ..." exit 3 and the normalized snapshots are lost (reproduced with --snapshot input). A crash or full disk mid-write truncates the previous snapshot file the analyst reuses offline.
defects.proposed_fix: Check the parent directory before planning requests (exit 2); write to a temp file in the same directory, fsync, os.replace.
defects.regression_test: tests/test_enrichment_review_regressions.py: missing parent is exit 2 before any opener call; a failing write leaves the previous file intact
